key_insight: PBRL can be made robust to heterogeneous and even adversarial annotators by explicitly modeling each expert's reliability and either trusting, ignoring, or flipping their pairwise labels during joint inference of the reward model. This yields reliable reward learning and downstream policies despite noisy or malicious feedback.
problem_solved: Preference-based RL methods break down when real-world pairwise labels come from mixed-quality annotators (accurate, noisy, or systematically adversarial); the paper addresses how to learn correct preferences and rewards when some experts cannot be trusted or actively mislabel.
method: Introduce a per-expert reliability model that classifies feedback into trust / ignore (don’t trust) / flip decisions and estimates flip probabilities for adversarial annotators.
Jointly infer true pairwise preferences and train the reward model (e.g., via a probabilistic preference model + EM or robust loss) while simultaneously estimating expert reliability parameters.
Use the inferred robust reward to train downstream RL policies and evaluate robustness across mixtures of honest, noisy, and adversarial annotators.
impact: Provides a practical way to use heterogeneous multi-expert feedback without extensive filtering or trusting all labels, improving robustness of preference-based reward learning and making human-in-the-loop RL deployment safer and more reliable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: annotators (honest, noisy, adversarial) → reliability estimator (trust / ignore / flip) → joint preference inference → robust reward → RL policy
Annotator reliability spectrum: icons for trusted, noisy, and flipped/adversarial annotators with estimated reliability scores
Performance chart: policy return vs. fraction of adversarial annotators comparing baseline PBRL, filtering methods, and the proposed robust method
Illustration of flip mechanism: example pairwise trajectory comparison where an adversarial label is detected and flipped before updating the reward model
paper_title: Trust, Don't Trust, or Flip: Robust Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Expert Feedback
paper_authors: Seyed Amir Hosseini, Maryam Abdolali, Amirhosein Tavakkoli, Fardin Ayar, Ehsan Javanmardi
